item.title: Alleged $2.1m land deal: Lawyers bicker over case against Wike’s son
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — Two senior lawyers have engaged in a war of words over the ongoing case concerning an alleged $2.1m Abuja land transaction involving Jordan Nyesom-Wike, son of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Jordan’s lawyer, Dr. Ogwu Onoja, SAN, accused Ibrahim Waru, counsel to the claimants, of distorting the facts of the case with lies which, he said, were aimed at tarnishing the reputation of his client, who, he said, openly denied any involvement in the alleged land racket during his court appearance. He insisted that his client neither had any transaction with the claimants nor admitted collecting the money. “This haze of lies and malicious fabrication appears to be an orchestrated media campaign intended to whip up sentiments, compromise the mind of the public and intimidate the judge. “For the record, Jordan Wike, in his defence before the court, stated in unequivocal terms that he has never met Safwan Garba G.Y. or any of his agents at any time. “He maintained this line of defence while giving evidence in court on 28 and 30 September 2026. One therefore wonders why a lawyer would grant interviews to misrepresent what transpired in court weeks after the proceedings. “It is baffling that this interview by I.G. Waru was granted this week at the Federal High Court, Abuja, close to a month after the proceedings at the FCT High Court. It is clearly the source of defamatory comments, unfounded claims and unproven conclusions being made on social media by ignorant members of the public,” Onoja, SAN, added in a statement he made available to journalists. However, reacting to the statement on Wednesday, Waru insisted that his clients are in possession of the signature of Wike’s son on the acknowledgement receipt for the $2.1m paid for the disputed land. In the statement titled “Re-joinder on the Press Statement Signed by Dr. Ogwu J. Onoja, SAN, FCArb, Lead Counsel to Jordan Nyesom-Wike in Respect of the $2.1 Million Matter,” Waru stood by his claim. The rejoinder read in part: “Having perused the statement signed by Dr. Onoja, SAN, for and on behalf of Jordan Nyesom-Wike, we found it necessary to respond, thus: “All that was stated during the interview granted by I.G. Waru Esq. was drawn from the hard record of proceedings and processes issued in suit No. FCT/HC/CV/008/2026, just like the signature of Jordan Wike on the acknowledgement receipt of the sum of $2.1m that he received from Safwan Garba GY on the 17th October, 2025. “The signature contained therein is the same as the one signed by Jordan Wike on his witness statement on oath before the court and, most importantly, the same as the specimen signature obtained from him in the witness box, after he was given a pen and paper and asked to sign five times. “Being a public document, it can be obtained by any member of the general public who, by virtue of Section 104(1) of the Evidence Act, applies for a copy.” Waru said the interview was granted to sensitise me

item.title: Fubara warns Rivers traditional rulers against partisan politics
item.description: By Daniel Abia, Port Harcourt Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has urged traditional rulers in the state to remain neutral in partisan politics, promote fairness and preserve peace in their communities ahead of the 2027 general elections. Fubara gave the charge on Wednesday while declaring open the 126th, 127th and 128th combined quarterly meeting of the Rivers State Traditional Rulers Council in Port Harcourt. He reminded the royal fathers that their primary responsibility was to administer justice, ensure fairness and promote peaceful coexistence, warning that their conduct should not create divisions or crises that could be difficult to manage. “As we are entering into this political season actively, everyone should ensure that your conduct promotes peace in your place. Your actions should not be what would lead to the division and multiple crises that we cannot manage as a government,” the governor said. He urged the traditional rulers to uphold the oaths and constitutional provisions they subscribed to before ascending their respective stools, stressing the need to protect the stability and progress of Rivers State. Fubara also called on them to set aside personal sentiments and place the interests of the state above individual considerations. “I want to enjoin everyone to keep aside issues of individual sentiments and ensure that the interest of our state supersedes whatever thing that we have in our mind,” he said. The governor added that prioritising the state’s interests was a principle he said had guided his day-to-day administration. On the welfare concerns raised by the traditional rulers, Fubara said delays in addressing some of their previous requests were not attributable to the state government but to the council’s inability to put its house in order. He explained that stipends paid to traditional rulers by local government councils were statutory benefits and not matters a governor could alter through verbal pronouncements. The governor, however, assured the royal fathers that he would fulfil his promises to them before leaving office next year. Fubara reaffirmed his respect for the traditional institution, describing its members as custodians of culture and tradition and an important link between government and the grassroots. He thanked the rulers for their prayers and support, urging them to ensure that the meeting produced fruitful deliberations capable of strengthening peace and development in the state. Earlier, the Chairman of the Rivers State Council of Traditional Rulers and Paramount Ruler of Apara Kingdom, Eze Chike Amadi Worlu Wodo, thanked the state government for maintaining a cordial relationship with the traditional institution. Wodo highlighted the role of traditional rulers in conflict resolution, noting that their proximity to residents placed them in a strategic position to mediate disputes involving chieftaincy matters, families and land ownership. item.title: Police arrest two over alleged kidnap plot in Kano
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Police Command has arrested two 20-year-old men over an alleged plot to kidnap the village head of Bangare in Gezawa Local Government Area of the state. The suspects, identified as Aliyu Naziru Garba and Bashir Alhasan, were arrested following a report that the traditional leader, Mallam Idris, had received threats of abduction. The Police Public Relations Officer, CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, disclosed this on Wednesday. Kiyawa said Idris reported the threat at the Gezawa Divisional Police Headquarters at about 1:30 a.m. on October 26, stating that an unidentified person had called him two days earlier and threatened to kidnap him. “Following the report, police operatives attached to the Gezawa Division launched an operation which led to the arrest of the two suspects,” he said. Kiyawa added that the suspects had confessed to the crime, while investigations were ongoing. He said they would be charged to court upon the conclusion of the investigation. The Commissioner of Police in Kano State, Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, commended the officers for their swift response and professional handling of the case. Bakori reiterated the command’s commitment to tackling criminal activities across the state. The police urged residents to remain vigilant and report suspicious persons or movements to the nearest police station. item.title: Ebonyi opposition protests proposed ₦150m billboard fee
item.description: By Anayo Okoli Opposition parties and residents of Ebonyi State have criticised a proposed ₦150 million fee for political campaign billboards, describing the measure as excessive and warning that it could restrict political competition ahead of the 2027 elections. The controversy followed a motion by the Deputy Chief Whip of the Ebonyi State House of Assembly, Hon. Arinze Lucas Chukwu, seeking to address what he described as the indiscriminate pasting of political posters and erection of billboards in the state capital. Opposition figures, however, argued that the proposed fee could make it difficult for parties and candidates outside the ruling party to publicise their campaigns. The governorship candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in the 2027 election, Dr. Kingsley Agbor, described the proposal as “unfortunate and devastating”. Agbor accused the administration of Governor Francis Nwifuru of attempting to restrict the political space for opposition parties. He said the proposed fee could undermine democratic participation and recalled the sacrifices made by Nigerians in the struggle to end military rule. “The government of Nwifuru once again wants to stifle the political space for the opposition political parties to operate. This is seen with this outrageous cost of elections and campaign billboards,” he said. Agbor alleged that the proposal reflected a desire to establish a one-party state, adding that opposition parties should not be silenced in a democracy. The governorship candidate of the Labour Party, Chief Splendour Oko-Eze, also condemned the proposal, describing it as an attempt to restrict opposition activities in the state. In an open letter, Oko-Eze questioned how opposition candidates would raise ₦150 million merely to erect campaign billboards and display posters. “Opposition is not a crime anywhere in the world. It is the beauty of democracy. It acts like a watchdog to the government in power so as to make sure that the dividends of democracy get to the people,” he said. He argued that the performance of an incumbent administration, rather than restrictions on opposition campaigns, should determine whether voters return it to office. Oko-Eze also questioned whether the proposed measure would apply equally to campaign billboards belonging to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). “How much did Governor Chief Francis Ogbonnaya Nwifuru and wife pay for all their billboards scattered all over the state? Or does it mean the law is just made for opposition parties and their candidates?” he asked. He urged lawmakers to ensure that legislation served the interests of residents rather than intimidate political parties and candidates. Also reacting, social media commentator and public affairs analyst, Chika Nwoba, warned that the proposal could heighten political tensions in the state. item.title: Senate seeks institution named after Fasoranti
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has called on the Federal Government to immortalise the late elder statesman and Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, by naming an educational institution after him in recognition of his contributions to education and national development. The Senate made the call on Wednesday while mourning Fasoranti, who died on October 20, 2026, at the age of 100. The lawmakers observed a minute’s silence in his honour and resolved to send a delegation to convey the Senate’s condolences to his family and the people of Ondo State. The resolutions followed the consideration of a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by Senator Adeniyi Adegbonmire (APC, Ondo Central), titled, “The Demise of Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, the Foremost Leader of Pan-Yoruba Socio-Political Organisation, Afenifere, and a Revered Political Leader from Akure, Ondo State.” Presenting the motion, Adegbonmire said Fasoranti left behind a legacy of service to humanity and significant contributions to Nigeria. Born on May 11, 1926, in Akure, Ondo State, Fasoranti had a professional background in education, which, according to the senator, influenced his approach to governance and commitment to human welfare. Adegbonmire noted that the late elder statesman established Omolere Nursery and Primary School and Akure High School, among other educational institutions, contributing to the development of education in Ondo State. He said Fasoranti emerged as leader of Afenifere after the death of Pa Abraham Adesanya. The senator also recalled that Fasoranti was a committed follower of the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo, leader of the Action Group during the First Republic, and later associated with the Unity Party of Nigeria during the Second Republic. He was also a founding member of the Alliance for Democracy. Fasoranti served as commissioner for finance in the old Ondo State under the administration of the late Governor Michael Adekunle Ajasin between 1979 and 1985. Adegbonmire described him as a respected elder statesman whose life was defined by service, integrity and commitment to the Yoruba people and Nigeria. He said Fasoranti was among prominent Nigerians who opposed military rule and advocated the restoration of democratic governance. The senator added that the deceased remained steadfast in the struggle for democracy, spoke truth to power and promoted collaboration among socio-political groups, including Arewa and Ohanaeze Ndigbo, in pursuit of a united and prosperous Nigeria. He said Fasoranti’s death marked the end of a remarkable era, but his legacy of principled leadership, wisdom and dedication to national progress would continue to inspire future generations. Adegbonmire also prayed for the repose of the deceased’s soul and strength for his family, the Afenifere organisation, Ondo State and the country to bear the loss. item.title: TUC rejects FG’s proposed ₦70,000 wage award to workers
item.description: Says govt has capacity to raise pay of lowest-paid worker to ₦300,000 By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — The Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) has rejected the proposed ₦70,000 monthly wage award for federal workers, which was agreed upon after a meeting between the Federal Government and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC). While rejecting the ₦70,000 monthly wage award, the TUC said the Federal Government has the capacity to raise the salary of the lowest-paid worker to ₦300,000 from the current minimum wage of ₦70,000, without waiting for a review of the minimum wage. In a statement jointly signed by Comrades Festus Osifo and Nuhu Toro, President-General and Secretary respectively, the TUC said that, in view of the prevailing economic hardship facing workers and the wider population, as well as the proposed measures to address it, what is needed is a salary increase and the implementation of the Joint Health Sector Union (JOHESU) Agreement. On the position of the TUC, it said: “Our position is unequivocal: workers are not asking for favours; they are demanding social and economic justice that protects their dignity and livelihoods. “The TUC will continue to defend workers’ rights without retreat, expose non-compliance and pursue every legitimate avenue to compel the government to honour its obligations. “Workers’ welfare is not a privilege. Agreements must be honoured. Workers’ rights must be respected. Government must comply. “The TUC therefore rejects inadequate temporary relief and demands wage justice for all categories of workers, social protection, reduction of the cost of living for the vulnerable, and full compliance with agreements. “The TUC therefore awaits the final outcome of the scheduled meeting with the government to decide on its next line of action.” It said temporary wage awards are not sustainable or far-reaching. “The wage award agreed between the Federal Government and organised labour on October 2, 2023, was to be implemented until a new minimum wage was agreed in 2024, but it was never implemented holistically. Some workers are still being owed one or two months, while others never received the award at all.” The trade union movement wondered why the government was returning to the same wage award that “never benefited all workers. How can workers be expected to trust fresh promises when previous obligations remain outstanding? “There was irregularity in the payment of the 2023 wage award, as those who even received up to four months’ wage award of ₦40,000 never got it every month, but at one- or two-month intervals and after several pushes. “Over 80 per cent of states and the informal sector never implemented any form of wage award. “From the foregoing, we further reiterate our demand for a pay raise for all government workers, as salary is the only consistent and far-reaching pay that workers can rely upon. “This was our position during the consultative interaction, and it remains our position today, as

item.title: Moonshot: Atiku woos founders, engineers; promises tax relief for startups
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has promised tax relief for young businesses and pledged to make government a major customer of Nigerian technology companies if elected president in 2027. Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), made the pledge in a post on his X handle on Wednesday, addressing founders, engineers and other technology professionals attending the Moonshot conference organised by TechCabal at the National Theatre in Lagos. He said young Nigerian companies have shown they can compete despite unfavourable government policies, and he promised to create a more supportive environment for innovation and business growth. To every founder, engineer, and dreamer gathered at the National Theatre in Lagos today for Moonshot by @TechCabal : you have built world-class companies in spite of policy, and I want to be the President who builds policy that works for you. I will give young companies tax… pic.twitter.com/VW8S37LhkB — Atiku Abubakar (@atiku) October 28, 2026 “To every founder, engineer, and dreamer gathered at the National Theatre in Lagos today for Moonshot by @TechCabal: you have built world-class companies in spite of policy, and I want to be the President who builds policy that works for you,” he wrote. Outlining his proposed support for startups, Atiku said young companies would receive tax relief during their early years, while government would use digital public services, budgeting and procurement to create opportunities for technology businesses. “I will give young companies tax relief in their early years. I will also make the government your customer by digitising public services, budgeting, and procurement, and I will require every new development to be fibre-ready,” he said. The former vice-president argued that Nigerian entrepreneurs had already demonstrated their capacity to build successful companies, saying government policies should help them achieve more. “You have proven what Nigerian talent can do alone. Imagine what it can do with a government on its side,” he added. item.title: Atiku to Tinubu: N70,000 allowance won’t end hardship
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has dismissed the Federal Government’s N70,000 monthly transport allowance for public service workers as an inadequate response to the rising cost of living, saying it cannot address the hardship facing millions of Nigerians. Atiku said the allowance, scheduled to begin in November, was a desperate attempt to contain public anger over the economic crisis, arguing that the government’s policies had made virtually every aspect of daily life unaffordable. In a statement on Wednesday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said the crisis extended beyond transport costs to food, energy, rent and other essentials, leaving households and businesses struggling to survive. “The Tinubu administration is scrambling from one announcement to another, showing its failure to grasp the crisis. The cost of living crisis reaches beyond transport: energy, food, rent and other essentials affect every part of daily life,” he said. Atiku illustrated the impact on ordinary Nigerians, saying, “Barbers pay more to power their clippers; restaurant owners face higher cooking costs; shopkeepers struggle to keep prices down; school bus operators pay more for fuel; and families still must buy food. Every business and household is affected. Does hardship end at the bus stop?” The former vice president questioned why the relief was restricted to public service workers when private sector employees, traders, small businesses, transport operators and millions without formal jobs were equally affected by rising living costs. “If public service workers receive N70,000 monthly for transport from November, what happens to private sector workers, traders, small businesses, transport operators and millions without formal jobs? The public workforce is only a fraction of Nigeria’s population. A temporary allowance for some cannot solve a national crisis,” he said. Atiku also faulted the government for failing to resolve the effective date of a new minimum wage, demanding clarity on payment dates, eligibility for the allowance and when wage negotiations would produce a decision. He said the six-month allowance would offer limited relief against soaring fuel prices, noting that N70,000 at about N1,400 per litre would buy roughly 50 litres of petrol. “What meaningful difference can 50 litres make over an entire month?” he asked. Atiku accused the Tinubu administration of creating the economic crisis through its policies and attempting to contain the consequences with temporary payments rather than address the underlying causes. “What Nigerians are witnessing is a government that set the house ablaze with its reckless policies, then pretends to fight the inferno by throwing ice cubes at the flames. A temporary N70,000 allowance cannot extinguish a cost of living crisis this government ignited,” he said

item.title: APC expands Tinubu campaign council with supplementary list
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The ruling All Progressives Congress APC has expanded the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu/APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council PCC with a supplementary list of directors and members spread across its directorates. The 11-page list names leaders and members for the sectoral groups, mobilisation structures and operational units of the council ahead of the 2027 general election. APC National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, announced the new appointments in a statement. He said the party “hereby releases a supplementary list of leadership and membership of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu/APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), expanding the composition of the Council ahead of the 2027 general election.” According to him, “the supplementary list contains additional appointments of leaders and members across various directorates, sectoral groups, mobilisation structures and operational units of the PCC.” The list is signed by the APC National Secretary, Senator Surajudeen Ajibola Basiru. Olorogun Festus Keyamo, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, is named Director of the Directorate of Air Transport Mobilisation. Mrs. Olubunmi Kuku is Deputy Director I, while Engr. Farouk Ahmed Umar is Deputy Director II. In the Directorate of Contact and Mobilisation, H.E. Yahaya Bello is named Deputy Director I, with Hon. Abdullahi Abdulkareem Tsafe as Deputy Director II. Senator Victor Ndoma-Egba is Deputy Director III in the Directorate of Manufacturing and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Sector Mobilisation. The directorate is headed on the list by Deputy Director II, Dr. Naomi Mcoliver. The Directorate of Artisan Mobilisation is led by Rt. Hon. Sanusi Garba Rikiji, Ph.D., as Director, with Rt. Hon. Chukuma Umeoji as Deputy Director I. The directorate also has zonal coordinators, deputy zonal coordinators and zonal secretaries for the geopolitical zones. Mr. Augustine Umahi is named Co-Director of the Directorate of Civil Society Mobilisation, while Senator Bayero Nafada is Deputy Director (Senate) in the Directorate of Parliamentary Mobilisation. The Directorate of Security and Intelligence has Gen. Tukur Yusuf Buratai and Chief Mike Okiro among its members. The Directorate of Entertainment includes Dauda Adamu Kahutu (Rarara) and Sani Musa Danja. The list also names three advisers to the Chairman: H.E. Ali Sa’ad, H.E. Senator Umaru Tanko Al-Makura and H.E. Saminu Turaki. The council’s principal officers are unchanged. President Tinubu is Chairman, with Vice President Kashim Shettima as First Vice Chairman and APC National Chairman, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, as Second Vice Chairman. item.title: Obi pledges emergency on security, education, power
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has promised to declare a state of emergency in security, education and electricity if elected president in 2027. Obi made the pledge on Wednesday during a town hall meeting with supporters and grassroots stakeholders in Kwanga, Nasarawa State, where he outlined his plans to improve security, expand access to education and boost electricity generation. The former Anambra State governor promised to deliver 10,000 megawatts of electricity within four years of an NDC administration, describing reliable power supply as critical to industrialisation and job creation. He criticised the administration of President Bola Tinubu, alleging that the president had spent more than 260 days abroad since assuming office while Nigerians grappled with economic hardship and insecurity. “Nigeria wants a leadership that will be available to all Nigerians, not a President that sits in Abuja or travels abroad while the country burns,” Obi said. On education, he promised free and compulsory schooling to ensure that every Nigerian child had access to education. Addressing the economy, Obi said borrowing was not inherently wrong but argued that loans should be directed towards productive investments rather than corruption and consumption. “Borrowing is not bad if you borrow for production, to build the economy. What is bad is when you borrow for corruption and for consumption,” he said. Obi also described the Obidient and Kwankwasiyya movements as groups united by a common desire for good governance and a change in Nigeria’s direction. He pledged to dismantle what he described as a cabal in the Presidential Villa that, according to him, had hindered the effective functioning of the Federal Government. The NDC candidate further claimed that his party’s presidential candidate and running mate were travelling across the country to engage directly with voters at the grassroots, rather than conducting their campaigns from Abuja. He thanked Nasarawa residents for supporting the vision of a new Nigeria, saying the movement for change remained alive. Also speaking, the NDC vice-presidential candidate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, described the party as one that belonged to all Nigerians and urged voters to participate actively in the 2027 general elections. Kwankwaso expressed optimism that the NDC would win Nasarawa and other states in the North, calling on Nigerians across party lines to support the joint ticket. In his remarks, the NDC chairman in Nasarawa State, Dogo Shammah, said the party was prepared to compete in the 2027 elections. Shammah described Nasarawa as Obi’s political home, attributing the claim to what he said was the level of support the candidate enjoyed in the state. item.title: 2027: Olisah Metuh, Ize-Iyamu join campaign council as APC releases supplementary list
item.description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) has added former Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) National Publicity Secretary, Olisa Metuh; former Edo State governorship candidate, Osagie Ize-Iyamu; and actress Foluke Daramola to President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 Presidential Campaign Council. The party announced the appointments in a supplementary list released on Wednesday, expanding the council’s membership across various directorates, sectoral groups, mobilisation structures and operational units ahead of the 2027 general election. The statement was signed by the APC National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka. “The All Progressives Congress (APC) hereby releases a supplementary list of leadership and membership of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu/APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), expanding the composition of the Council ahead of the 2027 general election,” the statement read. The party said the additional appointments were intended to strengthen coordination among the different components of the campaign council as preparations for the election continued. “Our great Party reiterates its commitment to ensuring effective coordination among the various components of the PCC as preparations remain in top gear for the 2027 general election,” the statement added. The supplementary list comes about two weeks after the APC released an earlier list of members of the presidential campaign council, which included opposition governors such as Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo and Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke. The latest appointments expand the party’s campaign structure as it prepares to seek Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. item.title: NAF to continue salaries until crash victims’ benefits are paid
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has assured families of personnel killed in the October 5, 2026, crash involving its ATR 42-500 aircraft, NAF 931, at Igbokoda, Ondo State, that their salaries will continue to be paid until their death benefits are fully paid to their next of kin. The assurance was given on Wednesday, October 28, during an engagement with the bereaved families to address their concerns and provide updates on the recovery operation and investigation into the accident. Representing the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, the Chief of Civil-Military Relations, Air Vice Marshal Edward Gabkwet, conveyed the service chief’s condolences and reaffirmed the NAF’s commitment to supporting the families. He said the Air Force’s responsibility extended beyond the immediate response to the tragedy. “The Nigerian Air Force stands with you, and our thoughts and prayers remain with every family affected by this tragedy,” Gabkwet said. As part of the welfare measures, Aneke directed that the salaries of the deceased personnel should continue until their death benefits had been fully paid to their next of kin. According to the NAF, the measure is intended to provide financial stability for dependants while the applicable benefits are being processed. The service said the policy reflects the Chief of the Air Staff’s emphasis on personnel welfare, including the well-being and security of their families. The meeting also provided an opportunity to update the families on recovery operations and the ongoing investigation. Gabkwet explained that the swampy, waterlogged terrain and difficult access to the crash site had posed significant technical and logistical challenges, requiring dewatering, engineering support and site stabilisation. He assured the families that the NAF would continue the recovery operation in collaboration with relevant agencies and support a thorough, evidence-based investigation. He said the service would not speculate on the cause of the crash until the available evidence had been properly examined. The NAF also facilitated engagements between the families and its religious leaders, including Christian chaplains and Muslim imams, to provide prayers, spiritual guidance and pastoral support. In addition, consultant psychologist, Professor Ehize Odigie-Okpataku, provided psychological support through individual interactions and counselling sessions. The families were given the opportunity to express their concerns and ask questions about the accident, recovery efforts and welfare arrangements. item.title: European gas prices hit 100 euros for first time since 2022
item.description: European natural gas prices climbed to the highest level since 2022 on Wednesday, topping 100 euros per megawatt-hour, driven by concerns over the Middle East war and the need to fill reserves ahead of winter. Around 1455 GMT, the Dutch TTF futures contract — the benchmark for European gas — rose more than four percent to reach 100.45 euros per megawatt-hour. Prices remain far below the peaks of the 2022 energy crisis triggered by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, when they reached 345 euros per megawatt-hour in March that year. The jump in gas prices on Wednesday reflected concerns that the United States could launch a new wave of strikes on Iran after next week’s midterm elections, risking a retaliation by Tehran on energy infrastructure in the Gulf. Exports of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from the Gulf remain very limited, according to analysts. “Concerns about renewed escalation in the Middle East are driving prices higher,” said Arne Lohmann Rasmussen, chief analyst at Global Risk Management. “However, weather forecasts are also providing support,” he added, as Europe is set for lower wind and solar generation, increasing demand for gas. Overall, European countries are consuming less gas than in 2022 as they increasingly switch to renewables to generate electricity. Analysts believe this shift reduces the risk of a gas price spike translating into hikes for electricity bills as severe as those seen in 2022. item.title: APC youths united under Dayo Israel, Obidike says
item.description: A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Chief Obidike Chukwuebuka, has dismissed reports of disunity within the party’s youth wing, insisting that it remains united under the leadership of its National Youth Leader, Hon. Dayo Israel. Obidike, a former aspirant for the position of APC National Youth Leader, spoke in Abuja on Tuesday after a strategic meeting of party youth stakeholders. He attributed reports of divisions within the youth wing to individuals uncomfortable with what he described as the unity and renewed mobilisation under Israel’s leadership. “As someone who contested for the same office and who understands the dynamics of the youth wing, I can tell you authoritatively that there is no crisis. “What we have today is a united, re-energised and focused APC Youth Wing. Hon. Dayo Israel has shown uncommon leadership, maturity and inclusiveness. He has carried everyone along, including those of us who contested against him. That is the hallmark of a true leader,” Obidike said. He said the youth wing had evolved from a party organ into a strategic electoral structure, with a presence across the country and in tertiary institutions. According to him, APC youths are now focused on mobilising support for President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general elections rather than engaging in internal disputes. “Our eyes are on the ball. Our principal, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, has shown courageous leadership in repositioning Nigeria. It is now the duty of we the youths to reward him with massive support. “I want to assure Mr President that Nigerian youths under the leadership of Hon. Dayo Israel are ready, mobilised, and will deliver no less than 15 million youth votes to secure his re-election in January 2027,” he said. Obidike urged APC youths across the six geopolitical zones to disregard reports of disaffection and continue to support Israel and the party’s leadership. “We are one family. The old politics of division is over. Dayo Israel is our leader and we are solidly behind him. Together, we will make history in 2027,” he added. item.title: 2027: Atiku will lose polling unit to Tinubu, APC declares
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Deputy National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Ali Bukar Dalori, has predicted that former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar will lose even his polling unit in Adamawa State to President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. Atiku, who is the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), hails from Adamawa State. Dalori, who spoke on Wednesday in Abuja at the graduation ceremony of women trained under the Tinubu-Shettima Village-to-Village campaign, also predicted that Tinubu would defeat Atiku in Borno, Yobe and other states in the North-East. “I don’t think that Atiku can disrupt the North-East. Why? Even Adamawa, his hometown, he will not win, even at his polling unit. I will assure you of that,” he said. Dalori said his prediction was informed by his experience as a grassroots politician and his understanding of the region’s political dynamics. He cited ongoing federal road projects as a major factor he believes would boost the APC’s chances in the region. The projects, he said, included the Gombe-Bauchi and Bauchi-Maiduguri roads, as well as the Maiduguri-Gamboru Ngala corridor linking Nigeria with Chad. He also referred to sections of the Maiduguri-Biu road that had previously been left incomplete, arguing that the continuation of such projects could strengthen the ruling party’s appeal to voters. Dalori said residents would consider the projects when deciding whom to support in 2027, adding that the contest should not be judged solely on Atiku’s place of origin or past electoral performance. In the 2023 presidential election, Atiku, then the candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), won Adamawa and other states in the North-East, while Tinubu secured the presidency despite losing several northern states to opposition parties. Dalori also defended the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms, particularly the removal of the petrol subsidy and changes to the foreign exchange regime, describing them as necessary measures to stabilise public finances and reposition the economy. He acknowledged that the reforms had generated debate and concerns over the cost of living but argued that they should be assessed alongside the administration’s infrastructure projects and other development initiatives. The APC chieftain also cited Vice-President Kashim Shettima’s origin as a factor he believes could strengthen the party’s prospects in the North-East. “Shettima is from Borno, from the North-East. He is our son. Because of that, we can do everything to ensure that Tinubu comes back for a second term,” Dalori said. Meanwhile, National Coordinator of the Tinubu-Shettima Village-to-Village campaign, Ambassador Farida Musa Jauro, pledged to mobilise more than one million votes for Tinubu across northern Nigeria through grassroots engagement and political sensitisation. item.title: Ebola: No gathering restrictions advised for Nigeria – WHO
item.description: By Dickson Omobola The World Health Organisation (WHO), Wednesday, said it had not advised the Federal Government to restrict public gatherings following the Ebola case recorded in the country. The organisation, however, said Nigeria would need to go 42 days without another Ebola case to be declared Ebola-free, while 53 people who had contact with the patient remained under surveillance. Speaking on Arise TV, Executive Director of the WHO Health Emergencies Programme, Dr Chikwe Ihekweazu, clarified that the patient’s medical evacuation was carried out at the request of her country of origin and was not due to any shortcomings in Nigeria’s capacity to manage the case. Ihekweazu also commended Nigeria’s response to the case, saying the speed of laboratory confirmation and sequencing, as well as the measures taken by the government to contain the outbreak, were commendable. He said, “We have advised the country to have appropriate response measures to this, and they have carried this out more or less to the letter. We have had excellent case management in Nigeria. Lab confirmation happened very quickly. We had the sequence happen very quickly. I think appropriate measures have been carried out. Nigerians can be proud of the response so far. We have not advised any restriction of further gatherings. Our advice is never political; it is always technical, and we will continue to support government in this response. “The key thing now is for every single contact that the patient had to be followed up with every single day, as is happening, to ensure that there is no further transmission. If there is transmission, it must be detected early and responded to appropriately. So, for now, I think the key thing is to keep this as a technical response, trust the government, and trust these agencies. They are being supported by the World Health Organisation in all ramifications of the response, and I am confident that we can support government to get this under control and not politicise this event at all.” In the period required for Nigeria to be declared Ebola-free, he said, “For certain diseases, a group of diseases we call the viral haemorrhagic fevers, of which Ebola is one of them, we consider every single case equivalent to an outbreak and requiring a coordinated response. In this case, that is exactly why we raised the alarm and supported the government to do what it needed to do to respond. Yesterday, we saw the medical evacuation on the request of the country from which the patient came. This wasn’t as a response to any deficit in the management capacities in Nigeria. item.title: [UPDATED] High-Speed Train Collision In Spain Kills 64, Injures Over 100
item.description: A high-speed train collision south of Madrid in Spain killed 64 people and injured scores more on Wednesday, with the toll likely to rise, authorities said in one of Europe’s deadliest such disasters this century. One train on the scene in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha was seen embedded into another after the second such accident to strike Spain this year. This still image from video taken and released by Spain’s Civil Guard on October 28, 2026 shows an aerial scene of a train crash between a high-speed Renfe AVE train and an Iryo train around 150 km south of Madrid between Urda and Los Yebenes in the province of Toledo. (Photo by Handout / Guardia Civil / AFP) Some carriages were lying on their side in tangles of metal debris at the bottom of an embankment, while dozens of emergency services vehicles were racing to and from the site. “We are speaking of approximately 64 (dead), but this is probably going to grow even more,” Castilla-La Mancha’s leader Emiliano Garcia-Page told reporters at the scene, raising a previous toll of 31. A spokeswoman from the Castilla-La Mancha government said that more than 100 people had been injured. Of them, 58 had been taken to hospital, with 15 in a critical condition. Helicopters hovered above the site during a frantic search for survivors, while several black vans arrived from a funeral parlour. State railway operator Renfe confirmed in a statement that the main high-speed line from Madrid to southern Spain had been suspended after one of its services suffered an accident with a train from private Spanish company Iryo. Iryo said in a statement that its train, which was carrying 147 passengers and five staff, including the driver, “was hit from behind” by the Renfe service. This still image from video taken and released by Spain’s Emergency Military Unit (UME) on October 28, 2026 shows military rescue personnel working at the scene of a train crash between a high-speed Renfe AVE train and an Iryo train around 150 km south of Madrid between Urda and Los Yebenes in the province of Toledo. Photo by HANDOUT / UME / AFP A visibly shaken Manuel Ortiz, 49, who lives in the nearby village of Urda, around 130 kilometres (80 miles) south of Madrid, told AFP he had been transporting survivors all morning in his car. Ortiz added that the passengers of the Iryo told him their train was stationary when the collision happened, describing a “horrific, horrible” scene that “smelled of an accident, of metal”. Rail Safety Under Scrutiny The accident comes one month before Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who faced heavy criticism for this year’s first disaster, seeks to overturn unfavourable polls and extend his eight-year premiership in an early general election on November 29. Sanchez’s office said he was heading to the scene. The premier had said on X that he was “shocked” by the accident and sent “my love, solidarity and support to all the victims and their families”.
